triggerPolicy: Every locked move with medium or low speaker-attribution confidence requires audio verification before adjudication.

source.description: Public YouTube 360p MP4 source containing English audio, acquired once with the existing local yt-dlp runtime; seven exact locked spans were extracted as mono MP3 verification clips.

checks.evidence: Diarization assigns the complete hemispherectomy, transplant, and fission trilemma to one dominant voice; a second voice is limited to the moderator's brief clarification about removing half the brain. The dominant voice is Crummett by first-person ownership of the stated argument.

One voice delivers Watkins's sustained Parfit-style reductionist account for 264.2 diarized seconds. A distinct voice begins Crummett's interruption only after 284.6 seconds, at the locked span's endpoint.

The dominant voice gives the first-person soul–body basic-causation defense and parity objection for 162.1 diarized seconds. Watkins's distinct voice supplies short prompts and restates his earlier empirical case before Crummett resumes.

The dominant voice gives the complete contingent-supervenience and conceivability argument for 152.8 diarized seconds. Watkins's answering voice begins only at the final 10.1 seconds, after Crummett expressly asks for his response.

After 2.05 seconds completing Watkins's dependence claim, the second voice gives 82.35 diarized seconds of first-person contingent-law and comparative-explanation argument. Its content and turn position identify that voice as Crummett.

Watkins's voice supplies 79.45 diarized seconds of the causal-closure, genetics, and animal-soul objection. Crummett's distinct voice is confined to the 1.75-second cats-have-souls interjection already described in the inventory.

Crummett's voice gives 86.2 diarized seconds of the basic-causation defense, explicit empirical concession, and parity generalization. Watkins's distinct voice states the conservation objection and begins pressing back at the end.

transcription.speakerResolutionMethod: Anonymous diarized voices were mapped from first-person argument ownership, explicit names, and verified handoff content in the frozen excerpts.

cost.pricingBasis: Recorded project pricing basis for gpt-4o-transcribe-diarize: $2.50 per million input tokens and $10.00 per million output tokens.
cost.explanation: The advance estimate incorrectly used a minute-based approximation. The diarized response's substantial labeled-text output made token-based cost materially higher; the measured usage is recorded and no paid call was repeated.
